subject: Per-token ladder: marginal vs blended breakpoints for GreenLeaf pilot
messages:
From: Tom Li <tom.li@greenleafhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@greenleafhealth.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Per-token pricing for hosted API pilot

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're finalizing our pilot economics and have one open question before procurement: how do you apply discounts on the hosted per-token model when we hit volume breakpoints? Specifically: do you use a marginal discount (only tokens above a breakpoint get the lower rate) or a blended rate (all tokens billed at the lower effective rate once breakpoint hit)? Also, how do commit tiers interact with the ladder — are commit discounts stacked with volume discounts?

We're targeting ~3B tokens over the pilot month (heavy generation + embeddings) and want to model both scenarios to compare against our in-house inference run cost. Can you share a concrete worked example and the typical breakpoints you offer?

Appreciate it —
Tom
Head of AI Partnerships
GreenLeaf Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Tom Li <tom.li@greenleafhealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-token pricing for hosted API pilot

Tom —

Great question and glad you're modeling this out. Short answer: we support both approaches in commercial discussions, but our standard public pricing is marginal (each band is billed at its band rate). For larger enterprise pilots we commonly offer blended/step-locked alternatives because procurement prefers simple unit economics for forecasting.

I've looped in Aditya (sales operations) and Marissa (your AE) to pull the exact breakpoints and a worked example based on your 3B token estimate. We can attach a simple spreadsheet showing marginal vs blended outcomes and two commit scenarios (no commit vs 1.5B committed tokens).

Are you available for a quick 20-min call Tuesday to walk through the numbers? If not, we'll send the worked examples.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, NA
Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-token pricing for hosted API pilot

Folks —

Attached is a draft worksheet (redwood-commit-summary.xlsx) with two tabs: Marginal_vs_Blended and Commit_Impact. Key assumptions I've used:
- Public base rate: $0.000020 / input token, $0.000030 / output token (we combine for an effective per-token rate in the sheet)
- Typical breakpoints we propose for hosted usage: 250M, 1B, 2.5B, 5B tokens/month
- Marginal discounts: 10% at 250M, 20% at 1B, 30% at 2.5B, 40% at 5B (applied to the band)
- Blended equivalents computed by taking total cost under marginal and dividing by total tokens to produce an all-in unit rate

Observations from the example for 3B tokens (sheet shows line-by-line):
- Marginal billing total = $X (see sheet)
- Blended equivalent once you cross the 2.5B breakpoint would drop unit price across all tokens ~12% relative to marginal outcome because of the wide band structure

Laura — can you confirm whether a 1.5B commit should be treated as a separate contractual discount that stacks on top of ladder discounts (we usually do stack but sometimes present it as an alternative for blended simplicity).

Aditya
Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-commit-summary.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 11:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-token pricing for hosted API pilot

Quick note on finance side —

We prefer to treat commit discounts as additive to marginal ladder discounts (so customers get ladder pricing on actual monthly volumes, and a contractual credit/true-up applied to reflect the committed tier). That keeps invoicing accurate and preserves cost incentives. For firms that insist on blended simplicity, we can produce an alternative blended proposal but it requires a slightly different revenue recognition approach and a 60-day billing true-up clause.

I'll draft two short options in the PD (commercial) template: (A) Marginal ladder + commit credit (our preferred) and (B) Blended all-in rate for forecast simplicity (requires true-up).

Laura Bennett
Dir, Finance & Pricing
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Tom Li <tom.li@greenleafhealth.com>, Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@greenleafhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Marginal ladder + 1.5B commit credit (GreenLeaf pilot)

Tom / Elaine —

Putting the numbers in one place for your procurement team (attached GreenLeaf_MAAP_Rate_Cards.pdf + the worksheet). High-level proposal: 
- Pilot expected volume: 3B tokens/month
- Pricing approach: Marginal ladder + commit credit (Option A) — you get ladder pricing on actual usage; because you commit to 1.5B tokens/month we apply a monthly credit if billed usage < commit (or invoice true-up if > commit).
- Example outcome (month with 3B usage): effective blended unit after credits = $0.0000186 / token (see attached calculation).
- Breakpoints used: 250M / 1B / 2.5B / 5B
- Next steps: If procurement is comfortable, we can spin a 90-day pilot MSA with this commercial schedule and standard SOC2 appendix.

Can you confirm whether procurement needs the blended all-in presentation (Option B) instead? If yes we'll re-run the sheet as an all-in quote with the true-up clause.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: GreenLeaf_MAAP_Rate_Cards.pdf, redwood-commit-summary.xlsx

1) For the commit credit, can you add a worked example in the MSA showing the monthly true-up math (we want to include it in our internal procurement checklist).
2) Do you offer a one-time onboarding credit to offset initial token surge during integration testing? Would probably be used in the first 30 days only.

If you can send the MSA commercial schedule and the additional worked examples by Wednesday, procurement can sign off and legal will run the SOW. We prefer Option A (marginal + commit credit).
